territorial_scope.description: Applies to internet application providers operating in Brazil, which must maintain a seat and legal representative in the country.

evidence.quote: Os provedores de aplicações de internet com atuação no Brasil devem constituir e manter sede e representante no país

summary.short: Brazil's Supreme Court partly struck down Marco Civil da Internet art. 19, which required a court order for platform liability for third-party content. Platforms are civilly liable in listed cases, including failure to remove listed serious crimes, and must meet notice, transparency and local-representative duties, from 5 Aug 2025.
summary.long: STF decision on Tema 987 (RE 1.037.396/SP), judged 26 June 2025, with embargos de declaração on 17 June 2026, declaring art. 19 of Marco Civil da Internet (Law 12.965/2014) partially unconstitutional. Internet application providers are civilly liable, jointly and severally under art. 21 of that law, for third-party content in cases of crime or unlawful acts, unless reasonable doubt on unlawfulness is shown after qualified diligence. Art. 19 still governs crimes against honour, email, closed video or voice meetings and private messaging. A relative presumption of fault applies to paid advertising, boosting and artificial inorganic dissemination mechanisms. Providers are liable for systemic failure to promptly remove content of listed serious crimes, such as anti-democratic acts, terrorism, incitement to suicide, violence against women and child sexual abuse material. Marketplaces answer under the Consumer Protection Code. Providers must adopt self-regulation covering notice systems, due process and annual transparency reports, offer user and non-user channels, and keep a legal representative in Brazil. Strict liability is excluded. Effects are ex nunc from publication of the 5 August 2025 minutes; the item 5 structural obligations run 60 days from publication of the 2026 embargos minutes.

notes: The document contains two decisions on RE 1.037.396 (Tema 987): the plenary thesis of 26.6.2025 [1] and the embargos de declaração thesis of 17.6.2026 [2], which refixes it. [2] is the later text; its wording differs in several items (item 3 adds 'de forma solidária'; item 4 changes 'rede artificial de distribuição (chatbot ou robôs)' to 'mecanismos artificiais de disseminação inorgânica'; item 5.6 is new; item 14 of [1] (prospective effect) becomes ex nunc from the minutes of 5/8/25 in [2] item 13, with a 60-day period for item 5 obligations in [2] item 14). The registry title also cites RE 1.057.258 (Tema 533), which does not appear in the fetched text. Relations to the MCI describe how the decision treats art. 19 and 21; the text itself amends or repeals no law.

thresholds.note: The decision (teses of 26.6.2025 and of the embargos of 17.6.2026) sets no numeric cutoff that changes the legal treatment of any person, entity, service or product. The numbers that appear were considered and excluded: the 60-day period for implementing the structural obligations in item 14 of the 2026 tese is a procedural time limit (event, not threshold); the date of the minutes (5/8/25) fixes the temporal effect and is not a threshold; statute and article numbers are citations; and the liability regime turns on qualitative standards (e.g., 'tempo razoável', 'tempo razoável', 'estado da técnica', 'dúvida razoável') rather than numbers. Penalties, fines and multas are referred to only generically, with no amounts stated.
